Subject: RE: Fwd: ClearFlow — sudden throughput collapse during peak window (11/08) — preliminary tech readout

Team — short tech summary from the incident triage:

Findings (prelim):
- Root signal: sudden token surge from customer jobs overloaded the reserved GPU slots' KV cache and pushed memory pressure on co-located partitions. We observed several runtime evictions followed by kernel fallbacks and increased GC cycles on quantized kernels.
- No model code push on our side during the window; this appears to be workload-driven.
- No disk I/O errors. Networking to the pool was stable; errors map to local process restarts and "OOM_recover" in the runtime logs.

Immediate mitigations executed (11/09):
- Rebalanced ClearFlow's traffic across their reserved nodes (manual routing weights) — reduced p95 by ~40% in the 30 min after change.
- Disabled low-memory optimized kernel for the affected model variant and forced fallback to a slightly higher-memory kernel that avoids the aggressive GC path (trade: +10% median latency, far fewer OOMs).

Recommended next steps (short-term):
1) Approve emergency burst: allocate +2 reserved slots for 2 hours to relieve memory pressure and prevent recurrence while we finish a deeper RCA. (Requires exec approval for capacity and potential credits.)
2) Authorize automated fallback policy for reserved pools: when eviction count crosses threshold, route to compatible hosted variant automatically (opt-in per-customer).
3) Engineering to add stronger KV cache telemetry and implement less-aggressive GC thresholds for quantized execution paths by EOW.

We can keep ClearFlow on the higher-memory kernel for now (they saw the p95 drop after rebalancing). If we get permission for a 2-hour burst we can eliminate the immediate SLA threat and buy time for a permanent fix.

I've attached a short runbook snapshot for the mitigations we ran.

Attachments: runbook_snapshot_20261110.pdf

— Irene Choi
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Vivek — short ask and recommendation below. This thread contains the customer impact details (attached traces/logs) and the infra readout.

What we recommend (combined plan):
1) Approve emergency allocation: +2 reserved slots (US-East) for ClearFlow for a 2-hour window starting on authorization. This is transient capacity from our Dedicated pool spare headroom.
2) Approve a one-time credit equal to 20% of the day's usage (to offset SLA exposure). Sales recommends this to preserve relationship and avoid churn.
3) Approve immediate opt-in for automated fallback routing (engineering will enable this per-customer guardrails) so customers can avoid SLA impact during noisy-neighbor events.

Risk/Cost notes:
- Headroom drawdown: short-lived, we have spare capacity but need exec OK for cross-account reallocation during peak windows.
- Financial: one-time credit is within precedent for top-tier accounts (expected ~$18k).

If you approve, Marissa will coordinate the customer comms and Irena/Irene will enact the slot allocation and routing change.

Please reply with simple "APPROVE" or "DECLINE" and any guidance.

— Aditya
